subject: paediatrics
title: Pediatric Neural Crest Tumours: Neuroblastoma, VMA, and Opsoclonus

steps.tx: Malignant transformation of primordial neural crest cells destined for the sympathetic nervous system produces the most common extracranial solid tumor of childhood. Typically presenting in toddlers under two years, **pediatric neuroblastoma** arises anywhere along the sympathetic chain, with sixty-five percent originating within the adrenal medulla. Tumors present as an irregular, firm, nodular, fixed abdominal mass that characteristically extends across the midline.
steps.say: Neuroblastoma is the commonest extracranial solid tumor of infancy, arising from neural crest cells in the adrenal medulla. It presents as an irregular mass crossing the midline.

vis.alt: Microscopic histology and CT scan showing Homer-Wright rosettes and a large calcified retroperitoneal neuroblastoma.
vis.caption: Histological demonstration of small round blue cells forming Homer-Wright rosettes in pediatric neuroblastoma. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Excessive catecholamine biosynthesis and catabolism by neural crest neuroblasts provide sensitive diagnostic and surveillance biomarkers. Over ninety percent of children with active neuroblastoma demonstrate elevated urinary excretion of **homovanillic acid and vanillylmandelic acid** (HVA and VMA), quantified on twenty-four-hour urine collections or spot urine ratios normalized to creatinine, serving as essential non-invasive biochemical markers.
steps.say: Elevated urinary vanillylmandelic acid and homovanillic acid occur in over ninety percent of neuroblastomas. These catecholamine metabolites provide sensitive tumor markers.

left.title: Biochemical Urine Catecholamines
points: Vanillylmandelic acid (VMA): end-product of norepinephrine
Homovanillic acid (HVA): end-product of dopamine
Urine VMA/HVA elevated in >90% of neuroblastomas
Normalizes with complete tumor resection; tracks relapse

right.title: Radioisotope Scintigraphy
points: Iodine-123 MIBG (Metaiodobenzylguanidine) scan
Taken up specifically by adrenergic sympathetic tissue
Detects primary retroperitoneal tumor and bone metastases
Gold standard staging and response evaluation scan

steps.tx: Histopathological evaluation classifies neuroblastoma among the small round blue cell tumors of childhood. Biopsy specimens demonstrate small, dark, primitive neuroblasts with hyperchromatic nuclei and scant cytoplasm, arranged in concentric circular rings around central eosinophilic neuropil, designated as **Homer-Wright pseudorosettes**. Immunohistochemical staining is characteristically positive for neuron-specific enolase, synaptophysin, and chromogranin.
steps.say: Homer-Wright pseudorosettes consist of primitive neuroblasts encircling a central tangle of pink neuritic fibers. Blasts stain positive for synaptophysin and neuron-specific enolase.

vis.alt: Comparative histological and imaging panel distinguishing neuroblastoma rosettes and calcifications from Wilms tumor.
vis.caption: Microscopic and radiological features distinguishing neuroblastoma from Wilms tumor and other small round blue cell neoplasms. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: A dramatic autoimmune paraneoplastic neurological disorder heralds occult low-stage neuroblastoma in young children. Known colloquially as dancing eyes and dancing feet, **opsoclonus-myoclonus-ataxia syndrome** (Kinsbourne syndrome) manifests with rapid, involuntary, chaotic, conjugate multidirectional saccades of the eyes, generalized myoclonic jerks of the trunk and limbs, severe cerebellar ataxia, and profound behavioral irritability.
steps.say: Opsoclonus-myoclonus syndrome features chaotic dancing eye movements, myoclonic jerks, and ataxia. It is an autoimmune paraneoplastic sign of occult neuroblastoma.

rows: Mandatory CT chest/abdomen to find tumor
Inability to stand or sit; severe truncal tremor
Persistent long-term cognitive and behavioral deficits

steps.tx: Extensive metastatic dissemination to periorbital bones and bone marrow produces pathognomonic physical signs. Retrobulbar orbital bone metastasis impairs venous drainage, producing proptosis and bilateral periorbital ecchymoses known as **raccoon eyes in neuroblastoma**. Extensive cutaneous subcutaneous metastases in infants present as bluish, firm nodules that blanch upon palpation, designated blueberry muffin baby lesions.
steps.say: Raccoon eyes with proptosis and periorbital bruising reflect orbital bone metastases in neuroblastoma. Infants may display bluish cutaneous blueberry muffin nodules.

left.title: Metastatic Skeletal Features
points: Raccoon eyes: bilateral periorbital ecchymosis + proptosis
Bone pain and refusal to walk from cortical metastases
Pathological fractures and cortical bone osteolysis
Bone marrow infiltration causing pancytopenia

right.title: Paraneoplastic Manifestations
points: VIP secretion: intractable watery diarrhea & hypokalemia
Catecholamine secretion: episodic hypertension & sweating
Opsoclonus-myoclonus-ataxia (dancing eye syndrome)
Horner syndrome in apical thoracic sympathetic tumors

steps.tx: Genetic amplification of the MYCN oncogene represents the single most powerful adverse biological predictor of aggressive neuroblastoma. Demonstrating **MYCN oncogene amplification in neuroblastoma** (greater than ten copies per cell detected by fluorescence in situ hybridization) strongly correlates with rapid disease progression, early metastatic dissemination, resistance to standard chemotherapy, and poor overall survival across all age categories.
steps.say: MYCN amplification with more than ten gene copies indicates aggressive high-risk neuroblastoma. It predicts chemotherapy resistance and poor survival regardless of stage.

steps.tx: A unique metastatic presentation in infants exhibits an extraordinary capacity for spontaneous regression without cytotoxic therapy. Classified under established staging criteria, **Stage MS or 4S neuroblastoma** is restricted to infants under twelve to eighteen months with a localized primary tumor (Stage 1 or 2) with metastases confined exclusively to the liver, skin, or bone marrow (with marrow involvement below ten percent), without cortical bone metastases.
steps.say: Stage 4S neuroblastoma occurs in infants with metastases limited to the liver, skin, or marrow. It can regress spontaneously through cellular maturation without chemotherapy.

left.title: Stage 4S Diagnostic Criteria
points: Age strictly under 12 to 18 months at diagnosis
Localized primary tumor (INSS Stage 1, 2A, or 2B)
Metastases limited strictly to liver, skin, and marrow
Bone marrow blasts <10%; cortical bone strictly negative

right.title: Biological Paradox: Spontaneous Regression
points: Non-amplified MYCN and hyperdiploid DNA content
Spontaneous regression into benign ganglioneuroma
Observe conservatively without cytotoxic chemotherapy
Gentle chemotherapy indicated only for respiratory distress

steps.tx: High-risk neuroblastoma requires an intensive multimodal regimen incorporating tandem autologous stem cell rescue and immunotherapy. Treatment incorporates intensive induction chemotherapy, maximal surgical resection, tandem autologous stem cell transplantation, radiotherapy, and targeted **anti-GD2 immunotherapy with dinutuximab** combined with granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor and oral isotretinoin (13-cis-retinoic acid) to eradicate microscopic minimal residual disease.
steps.say: High-risk neuroblastoma is treated with induction chemotherapy, autologous stem cell transplant, radiotherapy, and anti-GD2 dinutuximab immunotherapy with oral isotretinoin.

rows: Maximizes tumor cytoreduction prior to surgery
Delayed radical excision of primary retroperitoneal mass
Eliminates gross disease after vascular shrinkage
Vascular injury risk from encased vessels
